note: gold = fields the parser must output; omitted fields are unchecked
conventions: Gold lists only what the text states or clearly implies, never defaults. Lengths in metres, pitch in degrees; numbers are compared with 1 % tolerance.

Special expect keys: outOfScope (true = must be flagged out of scope, false = must NOT be flagged), unknownIncludes (words the parser must report as unknown, case-insensitive), why (the author's reasoning, never checked).

style is gold only when a style word or its translation is in the text (Baroque/barock, gotico, Jugendstil = art-nouveau, Roman/römisch/romano = roman, romanisch/roman (FR)/romanico = romanesque, ...). "Greek" inside "Greek Doric" is the order greek-doric (style unchecked). Landmarks (Parthenon, Alhambra, Kremlin, Pantheon) set only the field they map to.

A word that is both an order and a style (Gothic, Romanesque, Egyptian, Art Deco, modern) is gold as order on a column, pilaster, capital, base, pedestal, entablature, cornice or portico (style unchecked), and as style on every other element.
A pediment over/above a window or door: the element is that window or door, with the pediment field (the opening carries the dimensions).
dentils on a cornice or entablature -> cornice: dentils; on a moulding -> enrichment: dentils.
Italian "cupola" and French "coupole" mean a dome (element dome); English "cupola" is the small rooftop cupola.

colonnade / temple front / columned porch -> portico; corbel / bracket -> console; railing -> balustrade; pillar -> column; steeple / pointy church roof -> spire; astragal -> moulding with profile bead; quarter-round -> ovolo; cove -> cavetto.
slate on a roof -> covering slate (material unchecked); slate on a spire -> material slate. stucco/Stuck -> plaster; timber -> wood; gilded -> gold.

Out of scope: vehicles, animals, people, food, furniture (even "an Ionic sofa"), whole buildings (house, church, cathedral, skyscraper, Colosseum), nonsense, and architectural things the tool has no element for (staircase). An element of a building stays in scope ("church spire", "the dome of St Peter's").
Swiss thousands separator: 4'500 mm = 4.5 m (an apostrophe inside a number followed by a metric unit is not feet).
